topic: Overnighter vs multi-week trip: what changes in planning

content.hook: POV: your overnighter plan meets a 3-week route

slides.title: POV: your overnighter plan meets a *3-week* route
slides.body: What actually changes in planning when the trip gets longer.

slides.title: Overnighter: *pack light*, keep it simple
slides.body: One night means less food, fewer spares, and an easy bail-out. Plan the start and the camp spot.

slides.title: Multi-week: plan *resupply* and rest days
slides.body: Think water, food, repairs and sleep. Count realistic riding days, not just kilometres.

content.caption:
Overnighter vs multi-week bikepacking: what changes in planning.

Overnighter: pack light, pick a camp spot, keep a simple way home if plans change.

Multi-week: plan where you'll resupply water and food, where you can get bike repairs, and when you'll rest. Conditions change along the way, so plan by segment. Count realistic riding days, not just kilometres.

Either way, the basics stay the same: know your distance, your surface, and what the weather might do.

Which are you planning right now: overnighter or multi-week?
